<div class="markdown-body NewMarkdownViewer-module__safe-html-box__ZT1eD">

**What happened**:  
Running the [syft SBOM action](https://github.com/anchore/sbom-action) in a workflow generates an SBOM, but when combined with [scan action](https://github.com/anchore/scan-action) it did not produce any warnings, even though I purposefully put a vulnerable dependency in my project: <a href="https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Text.RegularExpressions/4.3.0" rel="nofollow">https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Text.RegularExpressions/4.3.0</a>

I downloaded the resulting SBOM artifact and scanned it locally, where I run grype version `0.73.1`, and this did not produce any warnings either.

I then generated the SBOM locally, with the exact same command as the action uses, where I had an older version of syft (`0.73.0`). When I then ran this SBOM together with grype, I get warnings as I would expect:

I then updated syft locally to `0.96.0` and scanned my codebase again, piping the SBOM to grype, and then I get no warnings at all.

**What you expected to happen**:  
I would expect the latest version of syft to work combined with the latest version of grype.

**Steps to reproduce the issue**:  
Create a dotnet project with a reference to package:

<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" snippet-clipboard-copy-content="&lt;PackageReference Include=&quot;System.Text.RegularExpressions&quot; Version=&quot;4.3.0&quot; /&gt;">

``` notranslate
<PackageReference Include="System.Text.RegularExpressions" Version="4.3.0" />
```

</div>

Build the project to get a `deps.json` file

Install syft `0.73.0`:

<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" snippet-clipboard-copy-content="curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anchore/syft/main/install.sh | sh -s -- -b /usr/local/bin v0.73.0">

``` notranslate
curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anchore/syft/main/install.sh | sh -s -- -b /usr/local/bin v0.73.0
```

</div>

Generate SBOM:

<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" snippet-clipboard-copy-content="syft packages -vv dir:. -o spdx-json &gt; syft.spdx.json ">

``` notranslate
syft packages -vv dir:. -o spdx-json > syft.spdx.json 
```

</div>

Run grype:

<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" snippet-clipboard-copy-content="grype syft.spdx.json

NAME                            INSTALLED  FIXED-IN  TYPE    VULNERABILITY        SEVERITY

``` notranslate

NAME                            INSTALLED  FIXED-IN  TYPE    VULNERABILITY        SEVERITY

```

</div>

Install latest syft version:

<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" snippet-clipboard-copy-content="curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anchore/syft/main/install.sh | sh -s -- -b /usr/local/bin">

``` notranslate
curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anchore/syft/main/install.sh | sh -s -- -b /usr/local/bin
```

</div>

Generate the SBOM again with the same command as previous generartion.  
Scan the file again:

<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" snippet-clipboard-copy-content="grype syft.spdx.json

No vulnerabilities found

</div>

**Anything else we need to know?**:  
I am not sure if this issue is for grype or syft, so I apologize if this is the incorrect place to raise this issue.

**Environment**:  
syft
